en: Majjhima Nikāya 93,
the Assalāyana Sutta:
Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, about five hundred brahmins from various kingdoms were staying at Sāvatthī for some business or other.
Then it occurred to those brahmins:
“This ascetic Gotama indeed proclaims purification for all four castes.
Who, then, is capable of engaging in debate with the ascetic Gotama regarding this statement?
Now at that time, a young brahmin student named Assalāyana was residing in Sāvatthī; he was youthful and had recently shaved his head.
He was sixteen years of age, a master of the three Vedas along with their vocabularies, liturgical formulas, phonology, and etymology—
the fivefold sciences including history— as well as a grammarian, an exegete, and one who had reached the limits of worldly philosophy and the marks of a Great Man.
Then this thought occurred to those brahmins:
“This young brahmin student Assalāyana resides in Sāvatthī; he is youthful, with a shaven head, sixteen years of age, a master of the three Vedas... [and] proficient.
He is capable of conversing with the ascetic Gotama on this matter.
Then those brahmins approached the young brahmin student Assalāyana; having approached, they said this to the young brahmin student Assalāyana:
“Master Assalāyana, this ascetic Gotama proclaims purification for all four castes.
Let Master Assalāyana come and engage in debate with the ascetic Gotama on this matter.
When this was said, the young brahmin Assalāyana spoke thus to those brahmins:
“Indeed, sir, the ascetic Gotama speaks in accordance with the Dhamma;
and those who speak in accordance with the Dhamma are difficult to counter-argue with.
I am not able to engage in debate on this matter with the ascetic Gotama.”
A second time, those brahmins said this to the young man Assalāyana:
"Master Assalāyana, this ascetic Gotama proclaims purification for all four castes.
Let Master Assalāyana come and debate this matter with the ascetic Gotama."
"But the conduct of the wanderer Assalāyana is indeed [well-known], sir.
A second time, the young brahmin Assalāyana said this to those brahmins:
"The ascetic Gotama, sirs, is a speaker of the Dhamma;..."
"Furthermore, those who speak according to the Dhamma are difficult to counter-argue with.
I am not able to engage in debate on this matter with the ascetic Gotama.
A third time, those brahmins said this to the young man Assalāyana:
“Master Assalāyana, this ascetic Gotama proclaims purification for all four castes.
Let Master Assalāyana come and debate this matter with the ascetic Gotama.
For it is indeed the way of life for you, Master Assalāyana, as a wandering mendicant.”
“May Master Assalāyana not suffer defeat in a battle he has not fought.
When this was said, the young brahmin Assalāyana said to those brahmins:
“Certainly, sirs, I do not prevail.”
"Indeed, sir, the ascetic Gotama speaks according to the Dhamma;
and those who speak according to the Dhamma are difficult to counter-argue with.
I am not able to engage in debate on this matter with the ascetic Gotama."
"Moreover, I shall go at the word of your honors.
Then the brahmin student Assalāyana, together with a large company of brahmins, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One.
When they had concluded their polite and friendly conversation, he sat down to one side. Sitting there, the brahmin student Assalāyana said this to the Blessed One:
“Master Gotama, the brahmins say this:
‘The brahmin caste alone is the highest caste; other castes are inferior.
The brahmin caste alone is the bright caste; other castes are dark.’”
“Only Brahmins are purified, not non-Brahmins;
only Brahmins are the true sons of Brahmā, born from his breast, born from his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, and heirs of Brahmā.
What does Master Gotama say about this?”
“Moreover, Assalāyana, there are seen among the brahmins brahmin women who are menstruating, those who are pregnant, those who are giving birth, and those who are nursing.
And although they are born from the very same womb as the brahmins, they say:
‘The brahmin caste alone is the best; other castes are inferior.’”
“The Brahmin alone is the fair complexion, while others are of dark complexion;
only Brahmins are purified, not non-Brahmins;
only Brahmins are the legitimate sons of Brahmā, born from his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, and heirs of Brahmā.”
“Even though Master Gotama speaks thus, nevertheless the brahmins here think:
‘The brahmin caste alone is the best caste; other castes are inferior … [they are] the heirs of Brahmā.’”

“What do you think, Assalāyana, have you heard that in the Yona-Kamboja countries and other outlying regions there are only two classes—the master and the slave; that one who is a master becomes a slave, and one who is a slave becomes a master?

“Yes, sir, I have heard that in the Yona-Kamboja countries and other outlying regions there are only two classes—the master and the slave; that one who is a master becomes a slave, and one who is a slave becomes a master.”
“In this matter, Assalāyana, what is the strength of the brahmins, what is their confidence, that they say:
‘The brahmin caste alone is the best; other castes are inferior...
[and so on] ...they are the heirs of Brahmā’?”
“Even though Master Gotama speaks thus, nevertheless the brahmins here think:
‘The brahmin caste alone is the best caste; other castes are inferior … [as before] … they are the heirs of Brahmā.’”
“What do you think, Assalāyana?

Suppose a kṣatriya were to kill living beings, take what is not given, engage in sexual misconduct, speak falsehoods, speak maliciously, speak harshly, indulge in idle chatter, be covetous, have a mind of ill will, and hold wrong view;
with the breakup of the body, after death, would he [go to] a state of deprivation...?”
Could it be that a brahmin would be reborn in a state of misery,
a fallen state, or in hell, while a vessa or a sudda would not—
given that both are equally one who kills living beings, takes what is not given, engages in sexual misconduct, speaks falsehoods, and uses malicious and harsh speech?
“Would one who is a speaker of idle chatter, covetous, ill-willed, and of wrong view, upon the breakup of the body, after death,
be reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, or in hell—
not a brahmin? “Certainly not, Master Gotama.”
For even a khattiya, Master Gotama, who kills living beings, takes what is not given, engages in sexual misconduct, speaks falsehoods,
speaks divisively, speaks harshly, indulges in idle chatter, is covetous, has a mind of ill will, and holds wrong view, might—
upon the breakup of the body, after death— be reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, or hell.
For even a brahmin, Master Gotama, ... [as before] ...
even a vaiśya, Master Gotama, ... [as before] ...
even a śūdra, Master Gotama, ... [as before] ...
"For indeed, Master Gotama, all four castes— if they were to kill living beings, take what is not given,
engage in sexual misconduct, speak falsehoods, speak maliciously, speak harshly, indulge in idle chatter, be covetous, have minds of ill will, and hold wrong views— would,
with the breakup of the body after death, be reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, perdition, or hell."
“In this matter, Assalāyana, what is the strength of the brahmins, what is their assurance, that the brahmins here say:
‘The brahmin caste alone is the best, other castes are inferior … [as before] … they are the heirs of Brahmā’?”
“Even though Master Gotama speaks thus, nevertheless the brahmins here think:
‘The brahmin caste alone is the best caste; other castes are inferior...
[they are] the heirs of Brahmā.’”
“What do you think, Assalāyana?
Is it only a brahmin who abstains from taking life, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from sexual misconduct,
abstains from false speech, abstains from malicious speech, abstains from harsh speech, and abstains from idle chatter?”
“...abstaining [from unwholesome conduct], free from covetousness, with a mind without ill will, and possessing right view, might, upon the breakup of the body after death,
be reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world, yet not as a khattiya, nor as a vessa, nor as a sudda? “Certainly not, Master Gotama.”
For even a khattiya, Master Gotama, who abstains from taking life, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from sexual misconduct,
abstains from false speech, abstains from malicious speech, abstains from harsh speech, abstains from idle chatter,
who is without covetousness, with a mind free of ill will, and possessed of right view— at the breaking up of the body, after death...
After death, one might be reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.
For even a brahmin, Master Gotama, ... [and so on] ...
even a vaiśya, Master Gotama, ... [and so on].
For even a *sudda*, Master Gotama … [and so on] … indeed,
Master Gotama, all four castes, when they abstain from taking life, abstain from taking what is not given,
abstain from sexual misconduct, abstain from false speech, and abstain from malicious speech, [abstain from harsh speech] … [and so on].
“Abstaining from speech, abstaining from idle chatter, free from covetousness, with minds free from ill will, and possessing right view—
upon the breakup of the body, after death, they would reappear in a happy destination, in a heavenly world. “In this matter, Assalāyana,
what is the authority of the brahmins, what is their confidence, that the brahmins here say such a thing?”
“‘The brahmin caste alone is the highest caste; other castes are inferior … [and so on] … they are the heirs of Brahmā’?
“Even though Master Gotama says this, nevertheless the brahmins here think thus:”
‘The brahmin caste alone is the highest caste; other castes are inferior … [as before] … they are the heirs of Brahmā.
What do you think, Assalāyana?
“Is it only a brahmin who is capable of developing a mind of loving-kindness—free from enmity and free from ill will—in this place, and not a khattiya, nor a vessa, nor a sudda?
“Certainly not, Master Gotama.
For a khattiya, too, Master Gotama, is capable of developing a mind of loving-kindness—free from enmity and free from ill will—in this place.”
For even a brahmin, Master Gotama...
even a vaiśya, Master Gotama...
even a śūdra, Master Gotama...
“For indeed, Master Gotama, all four castes are capable of developing a mind of loving-kindness—free from enmity and free from ill will—in this place.
“In this matter, Assalāyana, what is the authority of the brahmins, and what is their confidence, that the brahmins here say:
‘The brahmin caste alone is the best; other castes are inferior’ … [and so on]?”
‘an heir to Brahmā’?
“Even though Master Gotama says this, nevertheless the brahmins here think thus:
‘The brahmin caste alone is the best; other castes are inferior...’”
“An heir of Brahmā.
“What do you think, Assalāyana?
Is it only a brahmin who is capable of taking a bath-robe, going to a river, and washing away dust and dirt, and not a khattiya, nor a vessa, nor a suddha?”
“Certainly not, Master Gotama.
For even a khattiya, Master Gotama, is capable of taking a bath-robe, going to a river, and washing away dust and dirt; so too, Master Gotama, a brahmin...
and so too, Master Gotama, a vessa...”
"For even a *sudda*, Master Gotama...
indeed, Master Gotama, all four castes are capable of taking soapwort and bath powder, going to a river, and washing away dust and dirt.
"In this matter, Assalāyana, what is the authority of the brahmins, and what is their confidence, that the brahmins here say thus?"
“‘The brahmin caste alone is the highest caste; other castes are inferior...
[they are] the heirs of Brahmā’?
“Even though Master Gotama speaks thus, nevertheless the brahmins here think this to be so.”
‘The brahmin caste alone is the highest caste; other castes are inferior … [as before] … they are the heirs of Brahmā.
What do you think, Assalāyana?
In this case, a head-anointed kṣatriya king might assemble one hundred men of various castes and say:

"Come, sirs! Those of you who have been born into a kṣatriya family, a brahmin family, or a royal family, take a fire-drill made of *sāka* wood, or *sāla* wood, or *salaḷa* wood, or sandalwood, or *padumaka* wood, and produce fire; manifest heat."
"But let those venerable ones who have been born there into families of outcasts, hunters, bamboo-workers, cartwrights, or scavengers come forward;
taking a fire-drill from a dog-skin basket, a pig-skin basket, a dyer’s basket, or a castor-oil wood,
let them produce fire and manifest heat."
What do you think, Assalāyana?

Suppose fire were produced by taking an upper fire-drill from a noble family, a brahmin family, or a royal family, using as kindling wood from a *sāka* tree, a *sāla* tree, a *salaḷa* tree, a sandalwood tree, or a *padumaka* tree. Would that fire be such [as you described]?
The heat has been brought forth; is that indeed his fire which possesses flames, color, and radiance, and by means of which it is possible to perform the functions of fire?
But as for that [fire] produced from outcasts, hunters, bamboo-workers, cartwrights, or scavengers, using a dog-skin water-bag—
Or suppose fire were produced by taking a lower fire-drill from a pig trough, a washerman’s tub,
or a castor-oil wood; that fire would not have flames, nor color, nor radiance,
and it would not be possible to perform the functions of fire with such a fire.”
“No, Master Gotama. For even if someone, Master Gotama,

were to take a fire-drill made from the wood of a *sāka* tree, a *sāla* tree, a *salaḷa* tree, sandalwood, or a *padumaka* tree— belonging to a khattiya family, a brahmin family, or a royal family— and produce fire by friction,”
If its brilliance were brought forth, its fire would indeed be radiant, beautiful, and luminous, and it would be possible to perform with that fire whatever must be done by fire;
even if it were produced from a family of outcasts, a family of hunters, a family of bamboo-workers, a family of cartwrights, or a family of scavengers, [and placed] in a dog-skin water-bag.
Or, having taken a lower fire-drill from a pig trough, a washerman’s tub, or a castor-oil wood,
one produces fire and manifests heat; that fire would indeed possess flames, color, and radiance, and with that fire it is possible to perform the functions of fire.
"For indeed, Master Gotama, every fire has flames, color, and radiance, and everything that can be done by fire can be accomplished by it.
"In this matter, Assalāyana, what is the authority of the brahmins, and what is their confidence, that the brahmins here say:
'The brahmin caste alone is the best, other castes are inferior;'"
“Only the brahmin is the fair complexion, while other castes are dark;
only brahmins are purified, not non-brahmins;
only brahmins are the legitimate sons of Brahmā, born from his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, and heirs of Brahmā.”
“Even though Master Gotama speaks thus, nevertheless the brahmins here think:
‘The brahmin caste alone is the best caste; other castes are inferior … [as before] … they are the heirs of Brahmā.’”
“What do you think, Assalāyana?
Suppose here a kṣatriya youth were to have sexual intercourse with a brahmin girl, and as a result of that union a son were born to them.
That son born of a kṣatriya youth and a brahmin girl—would he be similar to his mother and similar to his father, such that he could be called a ‘kṣatriya’ or also called a ‘brahmin’?”
“Master Gotama, when a son is born to a kṣatriya youth by a brahmin girl, he might resemble his mother and resemble his father; should he be called a ‘kṣatriya’ or should he be called a ‘brahmin’?
“What do you think, Assalāyana?
Suppose here a brahmin youth were to have sexual intercourse with a kṣatriya girl, and from that union a son were born.”
“If a son is born to a brahmin youth by a kṣatriya maiden, would he be similar to his mother and similar to his father, such that he could be called either a ‘kṣatriya’ or a ‘brahmin’?
“Sir Gotama, if a son is born to a brahmin youth by a kṣatriya maiden, he would be similar to his mother and similar to his father, such that he could be called either a ‘kṣatriya’ or a ‘brahmin.
“What do you think, Assalāyana?”
“Suppose they were to mate a mare with a donkey, and from that mating a colt were born;
would that colt produced by the mating of a mare and a donkey be like its mother, or like its father, such that it could be called either a ‘horse’ or a ‘donkey’?
“It would indeed be a mule, Master Gotama.”
“For this, Master Gotama, I see a distinction;
but as for those others, I do not see any distinction whatsoever.
“What do you think, Assalāyana?”
"Suppose there were two young brahmin brothers born of the same mother; one was a student who had been initiated, and the other was not a student nor had he been initiated.
Which of these, O Brahmins, would you feed first at a funeral feast, a meal of rice-porridge, a sacrifice, or a guest reception?
"The one who is the student and has been initiated, Master Gotama—that is whom the Brahmins would feed first at a funeral feast, a meal of rice-porridge, a sacrifice, or a guest reception."
"For what reason, Master Gotama, would a gift given to one who is neither a reciter nor one who has been initiated bear great fruit?
"What do you think, Assalāyana?

Suppose there were two young brahmin brothers born of the same mother; one is a reciter who has been initiated, but is immoral and of evil character; the other is neither a reciter nor one who has been initiated, but is virtuous and of good character."
“Who, Master Gotama, would the brahmins feed first at a funeral feast, or at a meal of milk-rice, or at a sacrifice, or at a guest-offering?

“The young brahmin, Master Gotama, who has not studied the Vedas and has not been initiated, yet is virtuous and of good character—him the brahmins would feed first at a funeral feast, or at a meal of milk-rice, or at a sacrifice, or at a guest-offering.
For what purpose, Master Gotama, would a gift given to one who is immoral and of evil character be of great fruit?”
“First, Assalāyana, you went to [study] birth;
having gone to birth, you went to the mantras;
having gone to the mantras, you went to austerity.”
"Having gone to the four castes, I have returned to the purity that I proclaim.
When this was said, the young brahmin Assalāyana sat silent, abashed, with shoulders slumped, head downcast, brooding, and speechless.
Then the Blessed One, perceiving that the young brahmin Assalāyana was silent, abashed, with shoulders slumped, head downcast, brooding, and speechless, said this to him:
“In the past, Assalāyana, while seven brahmin seers were dwelling in leaf huts in a forest retreat, such an evil speculative view arose among them:
‘The brahmin caste alone is the best; other castes are inferior... [and so on].”
‘Heirs of Brahmā.
Now, Assalāyana, the seer Asita Devala heard:
‘It seems that such an evil view has arisen among seven brahmin seers who are dwelling in leaf huts in a forest retreat.’”
“The brahmin caste is the highest caste...
[they are] the heirs of Brahmā.
Then, Assalāyana, the seer Asita Devala, having trimmed his hair and beard and put on robes of madder-red color, [approached].
Having dressed himself in garments of *paṭali* cloth, put on sandals, and taken up a staff made of gold, he appeared upon the level ground before the seven brahmin seers.
Then, Assalāyana, the seer Asita Devala, while walking back and forth upon that level ground before the seven brahmin seers, spoke thus:
‘Where have these venerable brahmin ladies gone?
Where have these venerable brahmin ladies gone?
Then, Assalāyana, it occurred to those seven brahmin ladies:
“Who is this, appearing like a village headman, who is walking back and forth on the bare ground where the seven brahmin women sit and says:
‘Now, where have these venerable brahmin women gone?
Now, where have these venerable brahmin women gone?’”
“Come now, let us curse him!
Then, Assalāyana, the seven brahmin seers cursed the seer Asita Devala:
“Become ashes, outcaste!”
"You shall become ashes, outcaste!
However, Assalāyana, the more the seven brahmin seers cursed the seer Asita Devala, the more handsome, more beautiful, and more pleasing he became.
Then, Assalāyana, it occurred to the seven brahmin seers:
“Vain indeed is our asceticism, fruitless is our holy life.
For previously, when we uttered a curse—
‘O outcaste, become ashes!’— ”
“‘Ashes, outcaste! Be ashes!’—with this one indeed becomes ashes.
Yet, however much we curse him, he becomes even more handsome, more beautiful, and more pleasing.
“The asceticism of your honors is not in vain; the holy life is not fruitless.”
"Come now, sirs, abandon whatever ill will you have toward me.
"We shall abandon whatever ill will we have toward you.
But who indeed are you, sir?"
‘Have you heard of the seer Asita Devala?
‘We have, sir.’
‘Indeed, sir, that is who I am.
Then, Assalāyana, the seven brahmin seers set out to pay homage to the seer Asita Devala.
Then, Assalāyana, the seer Asita Devala said this to the seven brahmin seers:
“I have heard this, sir: it is said that among seven brahmin seers dwelling in leaf huts in a forest retreat, such an evil view has arisen:
‘The brahmin caste alone is the best caste; other castes are inferior.
The brahmin caste alone is the fair caste; other castes are dark.’”
“Only Brahmins are purified, not non-Brahmins;
only Brahmins are the sons of Brahmā, born from his breast, born from his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, and heirs of Brahmā.
“Yes, sir.”
“But do you know, sirs,
whether the mother who gave birth to you went only to a brahmin and not to a non-brahmin?
“No, indeed, sir.”
‘But do you know, sirs,
whether the mother of the mother of the birth-mother, and so on down through seven generations of maternal grandfathers, went only to brahmins and never to non-brahmins?
‘We do not, sir.’
“But do you know, sirs,
whether the father who begot you went only with a brahmin woman, and not with a non-brahmin woman?
“We do not, sir.”
“But do you know, sirs,
whether the father of your father’s father, back through seven generations of paternal ancestors, has always married only a brahmin woman and never a non-brahmin woman?
“No, sir.”
“But do you gentlemen know how the descent of an embryo occurs?
“We do know it, sir.”
‘Just as the descent of an embryo occurs:
here, when the mother and father have come together, the mother is in her season, and the gandhabba is present—thus, through the coming together of these three, the descent of an embryo occurs.
‘But do you know, sirs—’
‘Surely that gandhabba is a khattiya, or a brahmin, or a vessa, or a suddan?
‘We do not know, sir,
whether that gandhabba is a khattiya, or a brahmin, or a vessa, or a suddan.’”
‘This being so, sir, you should know: who were you?
‘This being so, sir, we do not know.’
"What are we? they asked.
Assalāyana, even those seven brahmin seers—when questioned, interrogated, and cross-examined by the seer Asita Devala regarding their own doctrine of birth—were unable to maintain it;
how then will you now, when questioned, interrogated, and cross-examined by me regarding your own doctrine of birth, maintain it, you whose teacher has not even mastered the basics?
When this was said, the young brahmin Assalāyana said this to the Blessed One:
“Magnificent, Master Gotama!
… [as before] … May Master Gotama accept me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forth for as long as life shall last.”
The Assalāyana Sutta, the third, is finished.
